quizName: DMV Practice Test #3 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: Which color should you wear to be more visible?
questions.explanation: Bright colors like orange, red, yellow, or green make you easier to see on a motorcycle. Wear bright clothing any time you ride, day or night.

questions.question: If you drink alcohol, you should:

options.text: Decide if you can ride safely based on how you feel after drinking.
Set a drink limit ahead of time so you can still ride safely.
Not worry about riding if you feel fine.

questions.explanation: Do not ride after drinking alcohol. Any amount of alcohol can affect your ability to ride safely.

questions.question: When riding, you should:

options.text: Look far ahead and watch for possible dangers.
Focus on the controls and speedometer instead of the road.
Not worry about hazards because there are very few on the road.
Look ahead but try not to look for hazards.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look far ahead and watch for possible dangers.
questions.explanation: Always look ahead to spot dangers early. This gives you time to react before you reach the hazard.

questions.question: To get the best protection, your helmet should:
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) and state standards. It should fit snugly all around with no damage.

questions.question: Motorcycle riders should choose shoes with soles that:
questions.explanation: Choose high, sturdy riding boots or shoes that cover and support your ankles. The soles should be hard, durable, and slip-resistant.

questions.question: To help other drivers see you, wear:
questions.explanation: Bright clothing helps other drivers see you. Wear clothes that increase your visibility day and night.

questions.question: When approaching a bump or pothole, rise slightly off your seat:

options.text: So you can jump off if needed.
So your legs can absorb the shock.
So other drivers can see you better.
So you can see the uneven surface better.

questions.correctAnswerText: So your legs can absorb the shock.
questions.explanation: Rising off the seat lets your legs and joints absorb some of the impact. This prevents the shock from throwing you off the motorcycle.

questions.question: A plastic face shield protects you from:
questions.explanation: A face shield protects your face from injury in a crash and shields you from wind, dust, dirt, rain, insects, and pebbles.

questions.question: Before riding, check your tires for all of the following except:
questions.explanation: Before each ride, check your tire air pressure, tread depth, and general wear.

questions.question: A way to lower crash risk is to:

options.text: Signal your intentions to other drivers.
Ride in positions where you are hard to see.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal your intentions to other drivers.
questions.explanation: Reduce crash risk by staying visible. Use your signals, brake light, and lane position to show other drivers what you plan to do. Keep space around your motorcycle and watch the road ahead, behind, and beside you.

questions.question: When passing parked vehicles, what should motorcycle riders be especially cautious of?

options.text: Drivers looking for a parking spot.
Cars pulling out of parking spaces.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cars pulling out of parking spaces.
questions.explanation: When passing parked vehicles, be careful. A car may pull away from the curb or parking space without warning.

questions.question: If hazards are on your left, where should you ride in the lane?

options.text: In the left portion of the lane.
In the right portion of the lane.
In any portion of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the right portion of the lane.
questions.explanation: When hazards are on your left, ride in the right portion of the lane to stay away from them. Change your position as traffic and road conditions change.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle on a slippery surface, what should you do?
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, reduce your speed. Use both brakes when stopping and avoid sudden movements.

questions.question: If another driver is tailgating you, what should you do?

options.text: Move to the side to let them share your lane.

questions.explanation: The safest way to handle a tailgater is to let them pass. Change lanes safely and allow them to go ahead. Speeding up only makes things more dangerous.

questions.question: Where should you find information about your motorcycle?
questions.explanation: Your owner's manual is the best source for information about your specific motorcycle. It covers how to operate it, its specifications, and maintenance needs.

questions.question: If you wait one hour for each drink before riding, what is true?

options.text: You cannot be arrested for riding after drinking.
Your riding skills will not be affected.
Alcohol effects may still affect you.
You will be fine as long as you ride slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Alcohol effects may still affect you.
questions.explanation: Most people eliminate about one drink per hour from their body. However, alcohol can build up in your system even with one drink per hour. This can still affect your ability to ride safely.

questions.question: What is usually found in the center of a lane?
questions.explanation: Cars drip oil and grease in the center of each lane. When it's dry, motorcycles can usually ride there safely.

questions.question: For the best protection, wear a helmet that:

options.text: Does not have a chin strap.

questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) standards. It should fit snugly all the way around with no visible damage.

questions.question: If a friend has drunk too much and wants to ride their motorcycle, what should you do?

options.text: Tell them to use quiet roads.

questions.explanation: Never let someone ride after drinking too much. Do whatever you can to stop them, including taking their keys. Find them another way to get home.

questions.question: For maximum protection, wear a helmet certified by which organization?
questions.explanation: For maximum protection, use a motorcycle helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) standards.

questions.question: During the day, you should:

options.text: Turn on your headlight only when it is cloudy.
Use your headlight if you think it helps.

questions.explanation: You should always turn on your headlight when riding, even during the day. This makes other drivers twice as likely to see you.

questions.question: Which type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead.

questions.question: A face shield:

options.text: Does not protect your face as well as goggles.

questions.explanation: A plastic, impact-resistant face shield gives the best protection for your eyes and face. Regular glasses or sunglasses do not protect enough. In Vermont, you do not need eye or face protection if your motorcycle has a windshield, but it is still a good idea.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Not wear a jacket if it is warm.
Always wear a jacket, even if it is warm.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always wear a jacket, even if it is warm.
questions.explanation: Always wear a long-sleeved jacket made of the right material when riding, even in warm weather. A jacket helps prevent dehydration. Always wear long pants and tuck in shoelaces so they do not catch on the motorcycle.

questions.question: The best lane position is:

options.text: The one that lets you travel the fastest.
The one that lets you draft off other vehicles.
The one that lets other drivers see you.
The one that puts you in other vehicles' blind spots.

questions.correctAnswerText: The one that lets other drivers see you.
questions.explanation: A good lane position helps you see others and helps them see you. It keeps you away from wind blasts, blind spots, and hazards on the road. Your position should stop other drivers from sharing your lane and give you a way to escape if danger comes. Choose a lane position that gives you the most space around you.
